title: Predictive vs Generative
goals: Distinguish discriminative prediction from generation by inspecting the requested output
Calculate an empirical next-token distribution from counted continuations
Separate next-token fit from factual support and downstream usefulness
vocabulary: A training aim concerned with producing or modelling possible outputs
A training aim mapping inputs to a specified target such as a label
Probabilities for alternatives given stated information
Producing a sequence one next item at a time using preceding items

worked_example.title: Generation continues after the first choice

blocks.text: After producing red, the next step conditions on the expanded prefix “The marker is red”. A second table might give an end token probability 0.8 and the token today probability 0.2. A generated sequence can stop at the end token or continue. Do not reuse the first-step table unchanged after adding a token unless the model explicitly ignores the new prefix.

A separate classifier can return red as a label from an image; that is a different input and target from continuing text. A downstream evaluation asks whether the system correctly reports the current marker. It must include ground truth or sources and appropriate failure handling, not just count plausible phrases.

guided_practice.title: Compute the distribution
guided_practice.prompt: For The marker is, calculate the three empirical probabilities, their sum and their meaning.
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: Probabilities 0.6,0.3,0.1 sum to 1 and describe ten supplied corpus continuations; they are not observations of the current marker.

independent_case.title: Analyse a new corpus independently
independent_case.task: For prefix The signal is, counts are high 2, low 5, unknown 3. Compute all probabilities and the most frequent continuation. A current measurement reports high. State what the most frequent continuation does and does not establish.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Probabilities high 0.2, low 0.5, unknown 0.3; low is most frequent. This describes the constructed corpus, not the current signal. Current high is supported by the supplied measurement; generating low would conflict with that observation.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: Autoregressive generation predicts the next item repeatedly.
The most frequent phrase is the current truth
Corpus frequency and current observations answer different questions.
A single accuracy score evaluates the whole system
Generation, retrieval, grounding, formatting and permissions require appropriate separate checks.

blocks.label: Write or draw your reasoning and evidence.

blocks.text: There are ten observed continuations. The empirical probabilities are red 6/10 = 0.6, blue 3/10 = 0.3, green 1/10 = 0.1. They are nonnegative and sum to 1. A simple frequentist classroom model uses these relative counts as its next-token distribution. These probabilities describe the supplied corpus counts, not the current colour of any actual marker.
